name: Finbud Financial Services Limited
sector: Retail credit distribution, digital loan origination and a young NBFC subsidiary
identity_note: NSE identity, SM series, 13 November 2025 listing and current issued shares reconcile to the IPO and annual report. Sources S1, S12 and S13.
summary: Strong underlying fee-platform growth is offset by weak cash conversion, specific control weaknesses and an unseasoned lender expansion. BQS 4.64; GQS 5.00 after the persistent-cash cap; IAS NS because the current funding and owner-value bridge is unresolved. The proposed subsidiary valuation is not cash.

quote.kind: Official closing price, not an executable quote

score_note: BQS 4.64; GQS raw 5.85 capped at 5.00 for persistent fee-platform CASH 3. IAS is NS because R and P are materially unresolved. No G1 or G3 failure override is applied.

gates.reason: Specific audited control findings and company responses require follow-through. Final IPO related-loan use scope remains unresolved; severe diversion or minority abuse has not been substantiated.

Historical audited parent financials and the restatement bridge are usable. The current NBFC capital, ownership and legal-entity cash bridge is insufficient for owner fair value. Classification differences are not called missing cash.

Restrained parent operations and an earmark-funded NBFC run-off survive without a new external raise. Actual bank headroom, preference maturity and current intercompany claims remain unverified. An unfunded growth case is not proof of essential-operation failure.
Eligible SM status and dated trades are verified. The 1,000-share lot and concentrated-activity cautions constrain execution. Suspension is not shown; actual position and live depth are unknown.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Finbud is primarily a fee-based retail-credit distributor, not a mature lender. Its Finance Buddha agency network and digital origination business generated almost all FY2026 revenue and profit. Group sales were ₹316.10 crore and PAT ₹11.65 crore; parent sales were ₹314.95 crore and PAT ₹11.62 crore. A young lending subsidiary, LTCV Credit, operates as Equall, while the newly incorporated ZAP subsidiary houses the digital expansion. The distinction matters: commission collection and agent advances determine the established business's cash economics, while loan losses, regulatory capital and funding maturities determine the NBFC's economics. [S1, S6–S8]

Verdict: Hold for evidence / high-growth fee-platform with cash and lender-expansion risk. BQS is 4.64, displayed 4.6. Raw GQS is 5.85, capped at 5.0 because fee-platform cash realization has remained weak after correcting the cash-flow classifications. IAS is NS: plausible funded parent returns do not establish current consolidated owner value when subsidiary preference terms, current bank availability and intercompany claims remain unresolved. This is not a finding of actual default or substantiated diversion. [S1–S7]

The strongest positive is genuine comparable fee growth: FY2023–FY2026 CAGR is 32.65%, supported by growth after agent commissions rather than merely larger pass-through revenue. The main negatives are thin core margins, a longer and capital-consuming collection cycle, specific control weaknesses, and a lending business without seasoned cohorts. The September announcement's ₹191.5 crore proposed subsidiary valuation is not realized parent cash or a verified fair value. Conditional base arithmetic is attractive, but the evidence does not justify promoting it to a purchase recommendation. [S1–S7]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff is 20 October 2026; the last exchange session is 19 October because 20 October is a market holiday. FINBUD trades on NSE SME, ISIN INE0EDU01014. The official ₹120 close and 19,049,480 current issued shares imply ₹228.59 crore market capitalization. Listing began on 13 November 2025. The 1,000-share board lot costs approximately ₹1.20 lakh at that close. These are dated reference facts, not an executable quote. [S1, S12, S13]

G1 is Conditional: specific control findings and related-party scope questions need follow-through, but the reviewed evidence does not establish severe minority abuse. G2 is Conditional: audited historical statements and the restatement bridge are usable; current subsidiary ownership and cash attribution are not sufficient for a reliable group valuation. G3 is Hold—unresolved: restrained operations can survive in the modeled countercases without an unreceived external equity raise, but actual available bank headroom, preference maturity and current legal-entity cash require verification. G4 is Conditional: dated trades and eligible SM status are present, but lot size and concentrated activity constrain execution. Status code 6 means price discovery, not suspension. [S1–S7, S12–S16]

Confidence is High for reported annual amounts, identity and the dated quote; Medium for comparable underlying growth, governance interpretation, cash-quality assessment and coarse liquidity; Low for a point current NBFC value and owner-return forecast. Historical confidence is not raised to defend an optimistic model. The user supplied no position size, holding constraints or portfolio exposure. Accordingly ₹5 lakh, a five-year horizon and a 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle are analytical reference assumptions, with 12% and 18% hurdle sensitivities, not suitability conclusions.

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 5, CAP 4, CASH 3, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 5. IAS uses Q 4.64, R NS, D 4, P NS and L 4. Each score reflects specific evidence rather than a neutral placeholder. Distribution scale supports activity, but not a high moat score; funded IPO resources support balance-sheet resilience, but not unrestricted-net-cash status; growth is strong, but cash realization remains poor. [S1–S7]

BQS equals 20% GOV + 20% MOAT + 12% REV + 10% DUR + 12% CAP + 10% CASH + 8% BAL + 8% EXEC = 4.64. GQS equals 40% REV + 20% DUR + 15% EARN + 15% CAP + 10% CASH = 5.85 before the explicit persistent-CASH override, giving final 5.00. The cash assessment is based on the fee business after separating NBFC funding and lien-deposit placement, not on applying a nonfinancial CFO/PAT test to a lender. [S1, S2]

REV starts at 9 because comparable CAGR exceeds 30%, but the four-year evidence window and Medium subject-specific confidence cap it at 8. No second small-base penalty or speculative forecast uplift is applied. IAS has 55% scored coverage and a known contribution of 2.36; its missing-weight interval is 2.81–6.86, not a point score. R and P are not reweighted away. BQS and GQS are eligible only for provisional quality comparison; IAS is not ranking-eligible. No governance or funding-failure cap is invoked, and no favorable investment classification is inferred from the model's conditional upside.

sections.title: 4. Business Model and Industry Economics
sections.text:
The established model earns fees for sourcing, matching and processing borrowers for banks and NBFCs. The agent channel provides physical distribution and documentation; the digital channel uses customer data, lender integrations and targeted marketing. FY2026 agency and digital revenue were approximately ₹273.4 crore and ₹41.5 crore respectively. Revenue includes accrued fees, not the principal value of loans disbursed. Disbursals and loan-book size must therefore never be added to revenue or mistaken for cash profit. [S1, S2, S6]

The core friction is timing. Finbud can pay agents after a lender records technical disbursement, while its own commission depends on final documentation and completion. Secured, balance-transfer and top-up transactions can take 30–90 days. Digital lending can also lengthen the bank's verification and payment process. This explains why an ostensibly asset-light fee platform needs agent advances, receivable funding and substantial working capital. It does not prove the advances are lost, but it does weaken a claim that growth is automatically cash-light. [S2, PDF94–98]

Revenue remains exposed to discretionary consumer-credit demand and lenders' underwriting appetite. In FY2025 personal-loan distribution accounted for 74.52% of parent revenue and business loans 20.81%; home loans were only 2.95%. The top lender contributed 20.10%, the top five 48.51% and the top ten 65.99%. Partners can reprice fees, build direct channels or terminate agreements. More than 100 lender relationships, as described by management, do not eliminate concentration in actual revenue. [S2, S7]

Equall adds a different risk pool: interest-bearing assets funded with equity and debt, subject to losses, maturity matching and regulatory capital. ZAP's April 2026 incorporation is an internal restructuring, not evidence of acquired growth. Marketing and subscription expense are real operating costs; a large customer database is not booked as a free, independently valued asset in this analysis. [S1, S7, S8]

sections.title: 5. Governance, Ownership and Minority Protection
sections.text:
The three promoters held 9,190,748 shares, 48.25%, at March 2026. Their absolute holdings increased from the prior year even as the IPO diluted their percentage, so a lower ownership percentage is not automatically promoter selling. The ₹71.68 crore IPO was a fresh issue. The June disclosure of a 1,000-share promoter-group purchase is small and not a substitute for cash-generation evidence. Current issued shares reconcile to the NSE master. [S1, S10, S13]

The FY2026 secretarial report identifies delayed structured-database entries, a former independent director's trading while the window was closed, a delayed ROC listed-status update, and temporary placement of ₹7.94 crore of GCP proceeds in an OD account contrary to the stated ICDR treatment. The board acknowledges the observations, describes strengthened controls, says the ROC filing was being completed, and records the OD amount's transfer to fixed deposits on 16 May. The June monitor subsequently places the restored amount in the monitoring account. These are specific findings with responses, not a generalized fraud accusation or a claim that ₹7.94 crore vanished. [S1, S3, S4]

The financial and internal-control audit opinions are unmodified. CARO separately discloses differences between quarterly bank working-capital submissions and books; the company attributes them to provisional management information versus final reconciliations. The report says there was no borrowing default. Audit comfort does not erase the specific reconciliation/control questions, just as those questions do not automatically invalidate every financial figure. [S1]

An additional scope question concerns ₹1.60 crore of GCP loan foreclosures, including ₹1.10 crore to Halfcute, identified in annual related-party disclosures. The monitor cites board approval, while the RHP contains a restriction on repayment of related-party loans from issue proceeds. The exact final-prospectus and approval scope must be reconciled before alleging any violation. Proposed management equity and later outside capital at LTCV also require a complete cap table, conversion and price bridge. GOV 4 reflects the mixed evidence; the severe governance override is not supported. [S1–S5, S11]

sections.title: 6. Competitive Advantage and Durability
sections.text:
Finbud's useful assets are its lender integrations, established agent network, borrower acquisition process and accumulated operating data. Agency partners can combine Finbud's lender access with local relationships, and digital retargeting can reuse an existing funnel across loan products. Management reports more than five crore customer records and believes this supports cross-selling and risk selection. The July update's 1,776 agents and strong digital activity are tangible evidence of distribution expansion. They do not independently demonstrate exclusive access, superior retention or lasting pricing power. [S6, S7]

Counter-evidence is material. Core group EBITDA, excluding interest income, was only 5.74% of revenue in FY2026. Agent commissions, marketing and subscription charges absorb most of the gross fee. Large banks can alter approvals and commission terms; agents and borrowers can use competing platforms. The FY2025 top-ten-lender revenue concentration of 65.99% and July 2025 concentration of 69.10% make partner quality and bargaining power more important than the nominal number of integrations. [S1, S2]

Management describes privacy consent, hashed identifiers and model-based targeting. These are attributed explanations, not an independent legal or cybersecurity assessment. The RHP disclosed no cyber-specific insurance at that time and no material breach then reported. This analysis neither assumes current insurance remains absent nor alleges unlawful data use. Future economics depend on lawful consent, security, lender acceptance and productive marketing spend, not simply the size of a data lake. [S2, S7]

My Mudra is a closer operating comparator for hybrid loan distribution than a full PB Fintech group multiple; BLS also has government-service exposure. The RHP's July 2025 peer prices are historical and its widely dispersed P/Es are not a current valuation anchor. Finbud must demonstrate its own retention, loss-adjusted returns and cash-backed unit economics. MOAT 4 and DUR 5 recognize a functioning franchise and runway while withholding a compounder label. [S2]

sections.title: 7. Growth, Comparability and Execution
sections.text:
Restated group revenue rose from ₹135.48 crore in FY2023 to ₹190.24 crore in FY2024 and ₹223.28 crore in FY2025, followed by ₹316.10 crore in FY2026. Comparable parent fee revenue grew from ₹134.93 crore to ₹314.95 crore across FY2023–FY2026, a 32.65% CAGR. FY2023 is used rather than the pandemic-affected FY2021 base, when the RHP says turnover fell below ₹50 crore. The tiny current NBFC contribution does not prevent scoring the established fee-growth trend. [S1, S2]

Gross versus retained economics are cross-checked. FY2026 parent fee revenue less agent commissions was ₹132.74 crore, versus ₹90.25 crore in FY2025, up 47.08%. That is not EBITDA: marketing, subscription, employees and other operating costs remain. Nevertheless, it supports expansion beyond a mechanical rise in commissions passed through to agents. FY2026 group core EBITDA increased more slowly than sales and the core margin was 5.74%, so strong revenue growth did not translate one-for-one into operating leverage. [S1]

The July management update reports Q1 fee revenue ₹83.2 crore, up 39%, with agency ₹67.5 crore and digital ₹15.7 crore. Digital growth was 116%, while total facilitated disbursals rose 49%. Q1 is a business update, not a complete audited quarterly profit/cash statement; the figures cannot establish current PAT, bank cash or cash conversion. [S6]

For FY2027 management targets approximately ₹425 crore revenue, ₹28–30 crore EBITDA and ₹18–20 crore PAT; its FY2030 aspirations are far larger. The model's ₹405 crore FY2027 base is an analyst assumption, not observed guidance delivery. A cautionary execution check is digital mix: the RHP described a 28% FY2026 aspiration, whereas the achieved FY2026 share was around 13%. Gold-loan and wellness cross-sell may help, but the new NBFC's ₹2,500 crore AUM ambition is not a funded forecast. REV 8 and EXEC 5 distinguish achieved fee growth from future execution. [S2, S6, S7]

sections.title: 8. Financial Quality, Cash and Capital Allocation
sections.text:
The RHP restated FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 group PAT to ₹1.8332 crore, ₹5.6578 crore and ₹8.4968 crore. The original figures were ₹1.4828 crore, ₹6.1541 crore and ₹8.3757 crore. Depreciation and tax adjustments explain the restatement. The FY2026 annual uses the original FY2025 comparative, so reported FY2026 PAT growth is 39.04%, or 37.06% against the RHP-restated comparator. Both are disclosed; neither series is silently spliced. Revenue is unaffected. [S1, S2]

FY2026 group PAT of ₹11.6456 crore includes ₹1.7768 crore interest income and a ₹0.4025 crore prior-tax provision reversal. A simple after-tax removal of interest and the reversal gives about ₹9.95 crore, before any further operating normalization. Current-share EPS is ₹6.11, versus weighted-average reported EPS ₹7.30. The current-share P/E is therefore 19.63×. An actuarial gratuity gain of ₹0.2798 crore also limits the repeatability of the reported employee-benefit charge; future cash-margin assumptions incorporate a more conservative benefits burden. [S1]

Parent CFO was negative ₹11.5051 crore in FY2025 and negative ₹7.7516 crore in FY2026. The latter includes ₹6.2593 crore placed in a liened long deposit under operating cash flows. Removing that placement gives negative ₹1.4923 crore; also separating the ₹2.9428 crore increase in the subsidiary reimbursement receivable gives positive ₹1.4505 crore. These are analytical diagnostics, not official restatements or a missing-cash allegation. Even that favorable correction is modest relative to parent PAT. Agent advances rose to ₹13.59 crore, and receivables to ₹44.36 crore. Ageing is mostly under six months, so slow conversion is not equated with defaulted receivables. [S1, S2]

The NBFC's loan-book funding is evaluated separately, not penalized through a corporate CFO/PAT ratio. A large idle IPO balance also distorts aggregate ROE and incremental-ROIC comparisons. CAP 4 reflects modest demonstrated reinvestment quality and unseasoned lender returns, not a fabricated negative incremental ROIC. CASH 3 reflects persistent fee-platform cash demand after the corrections; that supports the explicit GQS cap of 5. [S1–S4, S7]

sections.title: 9. Balance Sheet, Funding and Tradability
sections.text:
The parent March balance sheet totals ₹159.42 crore. Its ₹71.94 crore of bank cash and deposits is not unrestricted cash: the reconstruction assigns ₹3.92 crore current-account cash, ₹53.04 crore physical IPO cash and deposits including interest, ₹14.61 crore liened deposits, and ₹0.36 crore other short deposits. The March monitor's ₹60.71 crore unutilized-proceeds total additionally includes ₹7.94 crore parked in the OD account. That amount is not counted a second time as an asset. Restoring its separate cash location requires funding. June monitoring confirms ₹54.47 crore unspent principal in real deposits/monitoring cash, with separate interest. [S1, S3, S4]

The June remaining purposes are ₹13.52 crore working capital, ₹16.91 crore marketing, ₹14 crore LTCV investment, ₹2.04 crore specified debt repayment, ₹7.94 crore GCP and roughly ₹0.06 crore fees. Earmarked money can fund those purposes; it is not all unavailable, nor is it all surplus for dividends or unrelated promoter-loan repayment. Bank limits total ₹30 crore against March demand-bank drawings of ₹17.22 crore. The model explicitly draws restoration funding and any further existing-limit headroom, charges interest, pays term principal and retains collateral. Actual current covenant availability remains unverified. [S1–S4]

The opening claim audit maps parent TDS ₹6.8542 crore against current tax ₹4.0733 crore once; the residual is recovered or retained in sensitivity. It separately treats statutory dues, expense accruals, ordinary other liabilities, ₹4.9009 crore related demand loans, the ₹1.8412 crore rounded parent gratuity deficit, subsidiary reimbursement claims and contingent GST exposure. Deferred tax is not cash. Group preference capital is an outside subsidiary claim, not free parent equity. [S1, S2]

For liquidity, the ₹5 lakh reference takes about 5.3 sessions at 5% participation in the conservative recent turnover measure, approximately 13.3 at 2% and 2.7 at 10%. One absent observation is shown separately rather than proved zero trading. The ₹1.20 lakh lot is 24% of the example position. Active less-than-100-PAN and irregular-trading indicators apply from 21 October; they are cautions, not wrongdoing findings. L is 4, with live execution still unverified. [S12–S16]

The group also records ₹0.3526 crore more issue premium than the parent IPO addition, matching 5% of the outside preference face capital. Whether that premium belongs in a redemption or conversion claim depends on undisclosed terms. A face-plus-premium bound is retained rather than silently treating it as free common-owner value.

sections.title: 10. Valuation, Linked Scenarios and Implied Expectations
sections.text:
The dated parent model runs 67 monthly periods from the March 2026 balance sheet to October 2031, with investor entry on 19 October 2026. It links revenue, cash EBITDA, working capital, tax offsets, cash taxes, interest on drawn debt, maintenance/growth capex, mandatory term amortization, related-loan repayment, legacy gratuity, earmarked releases, subsidiary investment and dividends. No new parent equity or hypothetical rescue facility is assumed. Disclosed existing bank headroom is conditional on availability. Cash-flow checks prevent an IRR from being assigned to an unfunded path. [S1–S4; analyst assumptions]

The base assumes FY2027 fee sales ₹405 crore, progressing to an annual ₹812.51 crore run rate by the final period; cash EBITDA margin rises from 6.4% to 8.5%, working capital settles near 16% of revenue, and exit operating EV is 10× EBITDA. It funds within modeled disclosed limits with minimum parent cash ₹2.59 crore. Conditional terminal price is ₹423.04, producing 30.67% five-year annualized return including modeled dividends. These are not targets: current bank access, current opening roll and NBFC ownership remain uncertain. [S1, S4, S5, S7]

The bear assumes ₹335 crore FY2027 sales, slower growth, 4.5–5.2% margins and 20–22% working capital. Its peak gap is ₹7.26 crore, so no shareholder IRR is reported. The bull combines ₹425 crore initial sales, faster scaling, 10.5% terminal margin and 14× exit EBITDA; its upside is contingent on that demanding combination, not evidence of a likely outcome. A separate restrained-survival case is discussed below.

Base sensitivities include three extra working-capital percentage points, two fewer margin points, no existing-line headroom, no tax-credit recovery, no NBFC value and 7×/13× exits. A 15% hurdle corresponds to a conditional ₹222.70 entry price or 4.30× terminal EBITDA under the base's other assumptions. The low implied multiple is meaningful only if that growth and cash generation occur. The NBFC is valued through explicit conditional owner-book assumptions, not by adding 57.6% of the announced ₹191.5 crore. R and P remain NS. [S1–S7]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case, Lender ALM and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The credible failure mechanism begins with lenders tightening approvals or commissions while Finbud has already advanced cash to agents. Digital customer-acquisition costs may not fall in proportion to demand, and lender verification can delay collection. At the NBFC, higher-than-expected credit losses or insufficient eligible capital can interrupt new originations. Those risks can coincide, but this review does not stack arbitrary catastrophic losses merely to manufacture a failed gate. [S1, S2, S6, S7]

The restrained parent case cuts FY2027 sales to ₹285 crore, keeps margins near 4–5%, initially uses 22% working capital and maintains essential capex. It still provides the ₹14 crore earmarked subsidiary funding, restores the OD-located GCP proceeds with explicitly modeled financing, services claims and assumes no external equity raise. It survives with minimum parent cash ₹2.52 crore; conditional terminal value is ₹85.91 per share. This is a surviving countercase, not proof of current available cash. Conversely, the base with no usable remaining bank headroom has a ₹2.66 crore modeled gap, and faster growth with weaker collections exhausts disclosed limits. Optional growth funding failure alone does not establish essential-operation failure. [S1–S4]

A separate lender cash/ALM boundary uses the disclosed ₹5.3 crore March retail book, a bounded legacy-asset remainder, 25% loan yield, 14% debt cost and ₹2 crore first debt funding. It explicitly collects principal, recognizes loan losses, pays expenses/taxes/debt, and curtails new lending before inventing rescue funds. A stress version uses 7% annual loan losses, weaker legacy collections and hypothetical preference redemption at month 24. With the already earmarked ₹14 crore parent investment it survives; without that parent funding, restrained run-off reaches a ₹2.87 crore gap. Redemption timing and exact asset split are sensitivities, not disclosed maturities or adjudicated losses. [S1, S4, S5, S7]

Regulatory NOF is not identical to accounting equity. The RBI glide path and RHP describe ₹10 crore minimum NOF by March 2027 for this category; conversion and eligible-capital evidence are needed. The March retail book, subsequent disbursals and June ₹15.9 crore book also lack a complete public bridge. Therefore G3 stays Hold—unresolved, not an assumed pass, but neither is an actual default established. [S2, S6, S17]

sections.title: 12. 5× and 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A high revenue CAGR does not automatically produce fivefold or tenfold shareholder wealth. Finbud must retain economics after agent commissions, marketing and technology costs, fund receivables and lending capital, and avoid value leakage through subsidiary dilution or a poor exit multiple. The parent's share count is fixed only in the modeled cases, not promised permanently. Management's ₹1,000 crore fee-revenue and ₹2,500 crore NBFC-AUM aspirations are different quantities; AUM is neither revenue nor distributable equity. [S2, S5, S7]

At the base 8.5% terminal margin and 10× exit EBITDA, a first-pass fivefold share-price bridge requires approximately ₹1209 crore terminal annual revenue, implying 24.45% annual growth after the assumed ₹405 crore FY2027 base. Rerunning that path changes cash and working capital, yielding approximately ₹583, not exactly ₹600. The distinction is retained rather than falsely claiming an exact solver result. That path funds under the conditional bank/cash assumptions, but its margin and sustained execution still need evidence.

The analogous tenfold first pass needs roughly ₹2554 crore annual revenue and 44.53% growth after FY2027. Its rerun produces an approximately ₹83.3 crore financing gap with the existing structure. There is consequently no tenfold shareholder-return claim: additional equity or debt would alter ownership, interest and returns and cannot be assumed free. No IRR is assigned to that unfunded path.

The 5× outcome is an execution possibility under demanding funded assumptions, not the classification; 10× is unsupported by the present funding and evidence. The next useful proof is sustained cash-backed fee growth and mature loan-cohort economics, not a higher aspirational AUM number or an unreceived private-round valuation. [S1–S7]

An exact rerun also solves the terminal share-price crossings: fivefold requires about ₹1,249 crore terminal annual sales and 25.26% annual growth after FY2027, funded within the conditional model. Tenfold requires about ₹2,694 crore and 46.08% growth, with a ₹95.54 crore peak funding gap and no IRR. These are mathematical feasibility boundaries, not predicted outcomes.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan and Falsification Tests
sections.text:
The next full financial disclosure should reconcile fee revenue, bank receipts, agent advances and accrued commissions. The useful positive signal is not sales alone: it is higher retained fee income accompanied by cash collections and a stable or declining ordinary working-capital requirement. Rising prepaid commissions without equivalent completed lender payments, or repeated capital raising to cover ordinary costs, would weaken CASH and BAL further. Ageing should be assessed by due date and documented completion, not by calling every unbilled fee overdue. [S1, S2]

For Equall, require a complete post-allotment cap table, preference conversion/redemption terms, funds actually received, related-party balances, eligible NOF, maturity ladder and gross/net credit-loss cohorts. Reconcile March retail lending, legacy advances, Q1 disbursals and the June book. One-year seasoned vintages and collection performance matter more than an early 30/90-DPD percentage or an acquisition-funnel claim. If parent funding is delayed, rerun restrained operations before extrapolating ambitious loan growth. [S1, S5–S7, S11, S17]

Track the specified governance closures proportionately: the ROC status update, timely SDD controls, closed-window trading controls, charge registration and exact final-prospectus scope for GCP loan foreclosures. Preserve company explanations and official current outcomes; neither silence nor a late filing by itself proves fraud. For the GST disputes, distinguish the initial filed appeals from the annual report's statement that tribunal appeals were yet to be filed. [S1–S4]

Before any implementation decision, refresh the issued shares, board lot, current indicators, live depth and intended position. Recompute participation-based exit days for that position. This is a research checklist, not an automatic monitor, order or third-party outreach. A stronger investment classification would require the unresolved cash and ownership bridge first, then a rerun of R, P, G3 and the valuation sensitivities.

sections.title: 14. Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification remains Hold for evidence / high-growth fee-platform with cash and lender-expansion risk. The company has demonstrated real revenue expansion, but neither the governance, moat, cash-conversion nor capital-allocation evidence reaches the framework's compounder thresholds. BQS 4.6 and capped GQS 5.0 express that distinction. IAS is deliberately NS rather than a neutral score or an optimistic rerating based on an uncompleted subsidiary transaction.

The key unresolved investment question is whether cash-backed agency/digital earnings can scale while the NBFC remains adequately funded without impairing parent shareholders' economics. A lower share price can help only after the relevant cash, claims and ownership are understood. The conditional model's attractive base return does not override an unverified current opening position, and the bear's modeled gap is not evidence of an actual default. Both statements are necessary to avoid an artificially bullish or bearish conclusion. [S1–S7]

For a prospective investor, this is a diligence watchlist rather than a completed buy case. For an existing holder, the same evidence may inform a separate decision, but this dossier does not assume their cost basis, tax situation, concentration or ability to exit a 1,000-share lot. No portfolio weight is suggested from the illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity example.

The decisive evidence that could change the classification is a reconciled capital and claim bridge at LTCV, verified available parent funding and repeated fee-profit conversion after funding ordinary working capital. A new headline loan-book milestone without those improvements would not solve the problem. The research uses public information and conditional analysis; it does not execute any trade or commit funds.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text:
The source hierarchy is audited annual statements and restated IPO financial information for history; signed exchange filings for corporate actions; official NSE files for the dated quote, capital, series and turnover; and the original RBI framework for the cited NOF glide path. Management presentations, calls and business updates are clearly attributed. Monitoring reports verify specified uses from supplied evidence but expressly are not independent financial audits. Historical RHP peer figures are context, not current independent valuations. [S1–S17]

Decisive inspected material includes the annual group balance sheet, parent and group P&L/cash-flow notes, opening tax and accrued liabilities, loan schedules, related parties and preference capital; the RHP profit-restatement table; March and June IPO-cash tables; and the September conditional capital proposal. Scanned decisive tables were read with OCR and visual checks. The issuer website returned access errors for some pages; exchange and legitimate prospectus mirrors supplied the documents. No denied access was bypassed, and undated intake ratios were not promoted to verified financial inputs.

Analyst assumptions include forward cash margins, 27% cash tax, the timing of remaining TDS recovery, maintenance capex, ordinary working-capital ratios, interest on disclosed-limit drawings, term amortization, benefit payments, IPO releases, ₹14 crore subsidiary funding, restrained originations, preference-redemption sensitivity and 6×/10×/14× terminal operating multiples. Current shares, not weighted-average historical shares, determine per-share values. Restricted cash and owner claims are never silently counted twice.

Material open questions remain current legal-entity cash and usable bank limits; preference terms and actual conversion/allotment; the NBFC's complete asset, loss and intercompany bridge; exact final-prospectus loan-use scope; and current control-closure evidence. Small rounding differences and two-sided classifications are not treated as missing cash. These limitations explain specific NS investment factors while allowing evidence-based quality scores. The 20 October cutoff is fixed; later information is not silently included.

GOV.reason: Repeated specific compliance and reporting-control findings require improvement. Disclosed remediation, unmodified audits and the absence of substantiated diversion temper the assessment. Related-loan use scope and subsidiary ownership need evidence; no severe governance override is inferred.

MOAT.reason: Distribution and data scale are useful, but lender repricing and termination rights, low margins and absent independent switching-cost or retention evidence limit the advantage. A large data lake is not proof of superior credit underwriting.

REV.reason: Comparable fee revenue grew at 32.65% CAGR over FY2023–FY2026. The numerical band starts at 9, but four relevant years and Medium confidence cap the score at 8. Retained revenue after agent commissions grew 47.08% in FY2026 and Q1 fee sales grew 39%. The distorted pandemic base is excluded; no forecast bonus is applied.

DUR.reason: Retail-credit demand, cross-selling and digital adoption support a runway. Unsecured-credit cyclicality, lender concentration, regulation and unseasoned lending losses limit durability. The score is not derived from market size alone.

CAP.reason: Fee growth consumes working capital despite low physical-asset intensity. Post-IPO idle cash depresses aggregate ROE and is not automatically capital destruction. Digital unit returns and the NBFC risk-adjusted return remain unproven; no fabricated incremental ROIC is used.

CASH.reason: Fee-platform cash realization remained weak in FY2025 and FY2026 after separating the long liened deposit and incremental subsidiary reimbursement receivable. Agent prepayments and longer bank collections finance growth. This is not a corporate CFO/PAT penalty on normal NBFC loan origination. The persistent-cash GQS cap applies.

BAL.reason: IPO capital and disclosed bank limits provide a cushion, but deposits are restricted or earmarked. Related demand debt of ₹4.9009 crore and subsidiary capital needs require a dated claim model. The restrained parent scenario survives conditionally; this is not unrestricted net cash.

EXEC.reason: FY2026 fee growth and the Q1 update show operating delivery. Digital mix remained around 13% versus the RHP aspiration of 28%, and the new lending operation and control remediation remain unseasoned. Execution is mixed rather than absent.

EARN.reason: Most profit comes from fee operations, but interest income and the prior-tax reversal lift reported profit. Current-share EPS is ₹6.11 versus weighted-average ₹7.30, while restated historical comparators differ. Core margins and per-share cash progress are not yet compounder-quality.

R.reason: Returns are calculable only under conditional funding and subsidiary-owner assumptions. Current bank availability, preference conversion or redemption and intercompany claims are not reliably bridged, so a point expected-return score remains NS.

D.reason: Fee compression, collection delays and lending losses create a material permanent-loss path. The restrained scenario survives but loses value. A modeled expansion gap is not an actual default or automatic G3 failure.

P.reason: The current quote and issued shares are verified. A margin of safety cannot reliably be anchored to a proposed subsidiary-round valuation or unverified current cash claims. Conditional hurdle prices are not fair values.

L.reason: The ₹5 lakh reference takes about 5.3 sessions at 5% participation, starting at 5. One point is deducted for the ₹1.20 lakh board lot and concentrated activity. The live book is unknown, but a coarse historical score remains possible.

Q.reason: The exact unrounded final BQS is carried into IAS without a separate subjective adjustment.

GQS.cap_reason: Persistent fee-platform cash realization, CASH 3; not normal NBFC loan-growth cash flow.

ranking_eligibility.note: Quality comparisons use Medium-or-better factor evidence. IAS is not ranked until R, P and current funding are resolved.

model_limits: Parent fee-platform cash is modeled separately from NBFC. No group fair value is asserted.
NBFC loan/legacy-asset and preference conversion/reimbursement bridge is conditional, not audited fact.
GCP held in OD is not added as cash: replacement funding is explicitly drawn in May. Alternative no-draw case omits restoration and retains its restriction.
Parent TDS credit offsets current tax once; no gross tax payment plus duplicate credit. No deferred tax asset cash addition.
No current balance sheet after March or consummated September capital round verified. IAS R/P remain NS.
The no-GCP-restoration variant is a counterfactual financing sensitivity, not a claim that the disclosed May/June restoration did not occur or an acceptable way to avoid it.

Term principal uses disclosed current and long categories with a monthly allocation, not a verified lender-by-lender contractual calendar. An immediate repayment of the entire ₹1.1072 crore term balance also funds in sensitivity. A printed Oxyzo maturity preceding the balance date requires clarification; the audit reports no borrowing default, so an arrear is not inferred.

The subsidiary owner-book diagnostic and the separate lender ALM boundary are not one calibrated consolidated model. The bridge is deliberately unresolved; no group fair value or group IRR is certified.
